title: Judge rightly (John 7:1–24)
hookLine: at the harvest festival of booths, he teaches in secret then openly

lines: A HUT WITH A ROOF OF BRANCHES.
cards: Each autumn, Jewish families who keep Sukkot build a little hut: walls of wood or cloth, a roof of branches loose enough to see the stars through. For a week they eat in it, and some sleep in it.
It's called a sukkah, a booth, and the festival is Sukkot, the Feast of Tabernacles. Jews still keep it today.
Today's chapter of John opens as that feast approaches, and Jesus's own brothers are pushing him: go up to Jerusalem, show yourself to the world.

teach.h: TENTS IN THE WILDERNESS, AND HARVEST.
teach.b: "Now the Jews' feast of tabernacles was at hand." Tabernacle is an old word for a tent.
The law of Moses told Israel to live in booths for seven days, remembering the wilderness years, when God's people lived in tents and God kept them. It was a harvest festival too, full of joy.
John is honest about family: "For neither did his brethren believe in him." Jesus says his time hasn't come and stays behind. Then, after they leave, he goes up anyway, quietly, not openly.
In Jerusalem, people are whispering: he's a good man; no, he's leading people astray. Halfway through the feast, he walks into the temple courts and teaches out loud.
People are amazed: "How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?" He hasn't studied under any teacher they know. He's from Galilee.

They're judging by appearances, and he knows it. Then he takes up the sabbath healing again. You circumcise a baby boy on the sabbath, he says, when the eighth day falls on it, so the law of Moses isn't broken.
Why be angry with me for making a whole man well on the sabbath?
It's a careful argument from inside Jewish practice.

teach.h: JUDGE NOT ACCORDING TO THE APPEARANCE.
teach.b: And he ends: "Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment." A man from Galilee with no teacher might be a teacher. A healing on the sabbath might be keeping the sabbath, not breaking it.

how: Christians read this chapter as part of John's story of Jesus at the great Jewish feasts; Jews today keep Sukkot each autumn by building and eating in a sukkah.

games.q: your brothers tell you to go to the big festival and show yourself to the world. what do you do?
o: go with them and make a grand entrance.
stay behind, then go up quietly on your own.
games.why: he tells them his time hasn't come, then goes up "not openly, but as it were in secret," and teaches in the temple halfway through.

practice: Bring to mind someone you've judged quickly, by their clothes, their accent, their job, or one thing they said.
Then imagine what you don't know, what they carry, what they've survived, what they might be good at, and let your picture of them get a little bigger.
If you pray, ask to see them as God sees them; if you don't, hold them with more curiosity than you did a minute ago.

wordCard.voice: Sukkot. The Jewish feast of booths, kept each autumn, that this day's chapter opens as Jerusalem prepares for it.

orig.note: Greek: tent-pitching. John's word for the Feast of Tabernacles, Hebrew Sukkot.

carryVoice: Your line: judge not by appearance. The surface is only the start of a person. Until tomorrow.
